brief: J.P. Morgan's Flows & Liquidity update argues equity positioning and leverage excesses, which had unwound by end-July, have partly re-emerged (CFTC equity-futures leverage near YTD highs, SPY and semiconductor-ETF short interest bottoming, CTA momentum turning long Nasdaq/Kospi/Taiwan/Nikkei, leveraged-ETF AUM ratios rising, NYSE margin debt still elevated), posing a Q4 headwind for equities. It argues this headwind does not derail the tech/AI bull market because memory prices are rising, hyperscaler 2026/2027 capex consensus was raised to $805bn/$1.1tr from $758bn/$925bn, and AI compute (Hopper GPU) rental pricing is holding up. Separately, it argues bond fund inflows (running an annualized $1.7tr pace, above the $1.1tr its flow-return model implies) are partly a retail rebalancing response to strong YTD equity returns, but a negative duration impulse means these inflows are not capping yields, and its indicators show bond investors already positioned longer duration than desired. On FX, it argues spec investors are short EUR/long USD even as the euro trades firm, because corporate hedgers' past long-euro, short-dollar stance is now unwinding toward neutral, pressuring the euro down and the dollar up.
